missionPremise: OPS-16 A-149 (2026-09-14) ruled that county-to-serving becomes a program (P-186 through P-198) only after 'the adversarial teardown first' (OPS-24 section 3, step 1: 'Nothing else starts'), matching the 2026-09-10 CTX-teardown precedent's shape. This lane IS that teardown: a fresh planner, read-only, testing the program document and the map it was compiled from before any build row is dispatched, per the dispatch's own six-item test order.
completionPredicate: Done means: every 'exists' claim in OPS-24's stage table checked against source with a file+SHA and a verdict on whether its instrument can fail; the order tested for hidden forward dependencies; each of the six laws given one concrete violation, file+line, and an enforceability classification; each of the map's four holes verified at source; the 'what's missing' items classified as row/law/nothing; the Burnet choice checked against its own sources; and a review filed in the 2026-09-10 precedent's shape (theses, verdicts, evidence, what survives) so the overseer can amend OPS-24 from it before any build row is dispatched. All six items have at least one file-and-line-cited finding in the filed review; the two most load-bearing claims (the gate, the probe) were verified by direct code trace and, for the probe, by an actual offline self-test run, not by citation alone.
scopeBasis: Scope is exactly the dispatch's six numbered test items plus its explicit 'must not' list (no build, no farm design, no softened verdicts, no working-tree reads in the four product repos, no sub-agent). Live production/staging reads (gh/gcloud/psql/curl), which the 2026-09-10 CTX-teardown precedent used extensively, are OUT of scope here because this dispatch's read set is git-show/grep against origin/main only -- a deliberate narrowing from the precedent's shape, not an oversight, and named explicitly in CP1's methodology. One exception is declared and justified in the review and both checkpoints: scripts/surface-probe.mjs and scripts/tx-source-truth.mjs are doc_repo's own scripts (not one of the four product repos under the git-show-only rule), and were executed once each in their offline self-test/fixture modes (no network, no store write) because that is the most direct way to answer the mission's own instruction to 'run its instrument if it has one' for the one instrument central to Law 1.
